title: From Perez to David
intro: The book of Ruth closes with ten generations from Perez, son of Judah and Tamar, to David. Boaz stands seventh, an honoured place in a ten-name list, and Ruth the Moabite, a foreigner who chose Israel's God, becomes the great-grandmother of the king.
The same line opens Matthew's genealogy of the Messiah (Matthew 1:3–6) and appears in 1 Chronicles 2:5–15.
sources: Hebrew names: Miqra according to the Masorah. Ruth Rabbah; Babylonian Talmud, Bava Batra 91b and Sotah 37a; Rashi on Ruth 4.

people.note: Leader of the tribe of Judah in the wilderness (Numbers 1:7).
people.trad: The midrash: at the Red Sea, Nahshon was the first to jump into the water, and so Judah earned the kingship (Sotah 37a).

people.note: Matthew 1:5 names his wife as Rahab.

people.trad: Ruth is read on Shavuot: as Israel accepted the Torah, she accepted God's covenant ("your God will be my God"). The Talmud counts David's line from her (Bava Batra 14b).

people.note: "A son has been born to Naomi" (4:17): the neighbour women named him.
"A shoot will come forth from the stump of Jesse" (Isaiah 11:1).
people.trad: Counted among four who died without sin, only "through the serpent's counsel" (Shabbat 55b).
